_comment: Mutations for the Clerk webhook. It runs against the CLERK-mode pair because main.py mounts the webhooks router under Clerk only — on the local tiers the route does not exist and Python answers 404. Several of these are branches whose correct behaviour is to do NOTHING: not clearing a held past-due, not clearing a pending cancel, not touching an unknown plan slug. Those are the ones a port gets wrong by being helpful.

mutations.name: the signature is not verified
mutations._why: The whole security boundary. This endpoint moves an org's plan, so an unverified POST is a free upgrade for anyone who learns the URL.

mutations.name: a missing secret is treated as no verification
mutations._why: Refusing is the only safe answer: with no secret configured there is nothing to check a signature against, and accepting would mean the endpoint is open.

mutations.name: the dedup check is skipped
mutations._why: Svix retries on any non-2xx. Without the check a transient failure re-runs every side effect, and the cap re-evaluation is a read-then-write that can fire duplicate transition notifications.

mutations.name: only the svix- header is read
mutations._why: verify_svix accepts either namespace, so exactly one is populated afterwards. Reading only svix-id would silently disable idempotency if Clerk ever moved to the Standard-Webhooks names — the signature would still verify.

mutations.name: a paid snapshot clears a held past-due
mutations._why: The subtlest branch in the file. During dunning the item stays active with its paid slug, so clearing here resets the seven-day grace clock on every routine snapshot — including the ones this handler triggers itself via the member-limit PATCH. An org with a permanently failing card rides paid caps for free.

mutations.name: a canceled-but-paid item clears the pending cancel
mutations._why: Clerk emits subscription.updated alongside subscriptionItem.canceled. Only an ACTIVE paid item supersedes a scheduled cancellation; clearing on the canceled snapshot made the marker useless for a cancels-at-period-end banner.

mutations.name: a canceled item still inside its period is ignored
mutations._why: Clerk fires the cancellation the moment the payer clicks, but they keep the features until the period ends — and the snapshot taken right after that click contains only the canceled item. Ignoring it downgrades a paying customer on the spot.

mutations.name: a later canceled item overrides an earlier one
mutations._why: `entitled_canceled is None` means the FIRST canceled-but-paid item wins, matching the loop's order. Letting a later one overwrite changes which plan a multi-item subscription resolves to.

mutations.name: an active item no longer wins outright
mutations._why: The first active item returns immediately. Falling through collects it as a candidate instead, so a canceled-but-paid item elsewhere in the list can beat the one actually being paid for.

mutations.name: the past-due anchor is re-stamped every time
mutations._why: Clerk re-emits pastDue per dunning retry. Overwriting the anchor on each one restarts the grace clock every cycle, which is the same free ride as the branch above.

mutations.name: epoch milliseconds are read as seconds
mutations._why: Clerk's billing payloads are milliseconds. Read as seconds, a past-due stamped today lands in the year 57000 — outside what a datetime holds, so it is stored as a raw string and the grace maths cannot parse it at all.

mutations.name: the past-due keys are read as first-truthy-wins
mutations._why: `A or B` falls through to B whatever B is, including another falsy value. Both keys set to zero parses zero and stamps 1970; past_due_at alone being zero leaves None and stamps now. Reading it as first-truthy-wins gets the first case wrong.

mutations.name: an unparseable timestamp is dropped rather than kept
mutations._why: Python keeps `str(raw)` when the parse raises, so the operator can see what arrived. Falling back to now silently invents a grace window that nobody asked for.

mutations.name: an out-of-range timestamp 200s instead of 500ing
mutations._why: Python catches only TypeError and ValueError here. OverflowError and OSError — inf, or past the year an int can hold — propagate, and the difference between a stored string and a 500 is what Svix does next.

mutations.name: the member limit is never set
mutations._why: Clerk holds the seat cap, not this database. Without the PATCH a paying org stays capped at the free tier's two seats however much they pay.

mutations.name: an unknown item slug takes the free defaults
mutations._why: `item_slug in PLAN_MEMBER_LIMITS` means an unrecognised slug takes NO branch — it does not write a plan, and it does not drop the org to free. A bespoke Clerk plan would otherwise be demoted by its own activation event.

mutations.name: a period end assumes free instead of asking Clerk
mutations._why: One item ending is not necessarily free: a scheduled pro_plus to pro downgrade ends the pro_plus item while a pro item becomes active. Assuming free drops a paying org two tiers.

mutations.name: the org wipe leaves the database alone
mutations._why: This branch once cleared seven tables and left motion events, notifications, incidents, the outbox and monthly usage to outlive the org. It routes through the shared helper so a Clerk-initiated deletion and an in-app one reach the same end state.
mutations.new: let counts: Vec<(&'static str, i64)> = Vec::new();

mutations.name: a promotion to admin is only informational
mutations._why: Role escalation is the security-relevant case: a member-tier addition is routine, an admin appearing is the thing an operator needs to see.

mutations.name: the role prefix is stripped only from the front
mutations._why: `.replace("org:", "")` replaces every occurrence, not just a prefix.

mutations.name: a missing identifier does not fall back to the user id
mutations._why: The notification names who was added. Falling straight to "unknown user" when only the id is present throws away the one identifying thing in the payload.

mutations.name: the dedup row is written before the handler runs
mutations._why: A handler that raises midway must not record itself as done. Written first, a failed delivery is never retried and the plan change is lost — Svix sees the 500 but the marker says it is finished.
mutations.old:
// Recorded last, and only now: a handler that raised midway must
    // not mark itself done.

mutations.name: the cache is invalidated before the writes
mutations._why: Invalidating first leaves a window in which a concurrent reader re-primes the cache with the OLD plan, which then outlives the change by the cache's full TTL.

mutations.name: the segment caches outlive the camera rows
mutations._why: The caches are cleared before the cascade so nothing is left holding bytes for a camera that no longer exists.
mutations.equivalent: The write differential snapshots tables, and the segment cache is memory. hls_run.sh covers the cache but has no org-deletion case; the two harnesses do not meet here.
